name: Aoyama-Itchome
tagline: Roppongi in 3 minutes and Shibuya in 6 minutes. Served by 3 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥140,000 to ¥150,000.
summary: The station is in Minato City, where Tokyo Metro and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation run 3 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 13 minutes to Otemachi, 7 minutes to Shinjuku, 6 minutes to Shibuya and 20 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. The station stands 32.1 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 14.6 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 32.1 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 20.1 m to 34.7 m, a difference of 14.6 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, neither the station nor any of the nine points within 400 m of it falls inside the projected inundation area. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 10 clinics and 6 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is Sanno Medical Center, about 4 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 順和会山王病院, about 8 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 3 lines serve the station. Tokyo Metro Ginza Line run through it. Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line also call here. Toei Oedo Line are available too. The lines are split between operators (Tokyo Metro runs 2 lines and the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation runs 1 line), so when one line stops you can change to a line run by a different company.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Ginza Line runs at 153% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 赤坂見附→溜池山王, which this station is not on. Toei Oedo Line runs at 147%. Its busiest stretch is 中井→東中野, which this station is likewise not on. Tokyo Metro Hanzomon Line runs at 111%. Its busiest stretch is 渋谷→表参道, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥140,000 to ¥150,000 and 1K ¥170,000 to ¥180,000. 1LDK ¥300,000 to ¥310,000 and 2LDK ¥500,000 to ¥510,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. 3 lines and a wide choice of connections and a small projected flood depth pushes the figure up. On the other side, little daily shopping within walking distance holds it down. For 1K, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: rents are lower at Aoyama-Itchome, but Gaiemmae is ahead on the number of medical facilities and how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Aoyama-Itchome. Gaiemmae has only the Tokyo Metro Ginza Line, so Aoyama-Itchome is the better connected. To Shinjuku, for instance, Gaiemmae takes 7 minutes longer. A one-room flat also costs about ¥46,000 more at Gaiemmae. On the number of places to eat out, though, Gaiemmae comes out ahead.

neighbours.lead: rents are lower at Aoyama-Itchome, but Nogizaka is ahead on the number of medical facilities.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Aoyama-Itchome. Nogizaka has only the Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line, so Aoyama-Itchome is the better connected. To Roppongi, for instance, Nogizaka takes 14 minutes longer. A one-room flat also costs about ¥15,000 more at Nogizaka. On the number of places to eat out, though, Nogizaka comes out ahead.
